requirements.text: The command palette offers an 'Open file…' entry in every view. Choosing it launches the operating system file picker; the chosen files open in the editor and the main area switches to the editor view. The editor's existing Open… toolbar button, Ctrl+O shortcut and empty-state 'Open a file…' button keep launching the same picker.
tests: R1: the home view offers it and choosing it opens the picked file in the editor view
R1: the entry is present in the app view too, and cancelling leaves the view and tabs unchanged
R1: picking several files opens each one
R1: opening a file while another tab has unsaved text keeps that text
R1: the editor's Open… button, Ctrl+O and the empty-state button still run the same picker

requirements.text: The sidebar contains a Files explorer section beside the apps list (a second section or a tab; the layout is the builder's choice). It shows a tree that loads one directory level at a time: clicking a folder expands or collapses it, and its children are fetched only when it is first expanded. By default the tree hides the folders named node_modules, .git, target and dist; a Show hidden control reveals them and hides them again. A folder that cannot be read appears as locked and does not raise an error.
tests: r2_lists_one_level_and_tells_folders_from_files
r2_children_are_fetched_only_when_their_level_is_requested
r2_hides_the_four_noisy_names_by_default_at_any_depth
r2_show_hidden_reveals_the_four_names_and_can_hide_them_again
r2_other_dot_named_entries_are_listed_normally
r2_an_empty_folder_lists_no_children_without_error
r2_an_unreadable_folder_is_locked_and_does_not_raise
a1_a_large_level_is_capped_with_total_and_truncated
a1_folders_come_first_then_files_sorted_by_name
a1_scanning_stops_at_the_scan_limit
R2 lists one level through explorer_list, passing the folder and camelCase showHidden
R2 asks for the same folder with showHidden off when hidden names are hidden
R2 reads exactly one level: only the root folder, never its descendants
R2 a folder's children are requested only when it is first expanded, and not again
R2 toggling Show hidden re-reads the shown levels with the hidden names on, and off again
R2 a folder that cannot be read becomes a locked level instead of a thrown error
A1 keeps the visible total and truncated flag and does not re-read a level on re-render
A1 caches at most 100 levels and evicts the least recently used
R2 lists one level and distinguishes folders from files
R2 clicking a folder expands it, fetching its children only then, and clicking again collapses it
R2 an empty folder expands without error and shows no children
R2 a large folder shows a loading indication while it reads
R2 a folder that cannot be read shows as locked instead of throwing
R2 other dot-named files and folders are listed normally
R2 Show hidden turns the hidden names on and off again
A1 says when a level is truncated: Showing first 1000 of 1200
A3 with no explorer prop the apps, Home row and rail are exactly as before
R2 the Files section sits beside the apps list when one is given
A3 the collapsed rail never shows the Files section
R2: it sits beside the apps list in the expanded pane
A3: with no explorer prop the app rows and Home row are exactly as before
A3: the collapsed rail never shows the Files section
A2: package.json, package-lock.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and tauri.conf.json all say 2.2.0

requirements.text: Clicking a file in the explorer opens it through the editor's existing open path and switches the main area to the editor view. If the file is already open, its existing tab is focused instead of opening a second tab. Images and other preview-kind files follow the editor's existing preview handling.
tests: R3 clicking a file hands it to the editor's existing open path and never reads it as a folder
R3 a file that is already open still goes through the same single open path
R3 clicking a folder only expands it and never opens it as a file
R3 a click reaches the editor controller's openPath, the same editor_open_any the picker uses
R3: clicking a file opens it through the editor's open path and shows the editor view
R3: clicking a file that is already open focuses its tab instead of opening a second
R3: a file that fails to open shows the editor's existing error instead of crashing
R3: clicking a folder expands it and never opens it as a file

requirements.text: The explorer root follows where the user is. In the app view the root is the selected app's root. In the editor view it is the root of the app that owns the active editor tab, found with the same path-to-owning-app lookup the tab groups use (the deepest app root that contains the path). The user never chooses a root by hand when an app root applies. Changing the root never closes or changes any open tab.
tests: r4_a_missing_app_root_is_locked_instead_of_raising
R4 in the app view the root is the selected app's root
R4 switching to another app moves the root
R4 in the editor view the root is the app that owns the active tab
R4 with nested roots the deepest root containing the file owns it
R4 opening a file under the current root keeps the same owning app
R4 a file outside every app root is not guessed into the nearest app
R4 a path written with other slashes or case still finds its owner
R4 an app with no root has nothing to show
A5 the home view has no root, so the panel shows a hint
A5 an editor view with no tab, or an unsaved tab, has no root
R4 an app root offers no Up, so its top folder stays the app root
R4/R5 a change of view, app or active tab discards Up navigation and returns to the automatic root
A5 with no root nothing applies, so no folder is read
R4 an app root offers no Up, so the top folder stays the app root
R4 switching the selected app or tab changes the root without touching any tab
R4 if an app's root no longer exists it shows as locked instead of raising an error
A5 with no root it shows a hint and asks the core for nothing
R4: in the app view it is the selected app's root and follows a newly selected app
R4: in the editor view it is the deepest owning app's root
R4: opening a file under the current root keeps the same owning app, so the root does not jump
R4: an app root that no longer exists shows as unreadable instead of raising

requirements.text: When the active editor tab belongs to no app (the Misc group), for example a loose file opened through 'Edit with Tinkerdeck' from outside every app root, the explorer is rooted at that file's parent folder, and Up climbs the folder hierarchy all the way to the drive list.
tests: r5_drives_are_listed_as_drive_roots
R5 a Misc file roots at its parent folder, not the home folder
R5 a Misc file at the root of a drive roots at that drive and Up reaches the drive list
R5 Up climbs one folder at a time up to the drive list
R5 switching between two Misc files moves the root
R5 switching from an app-owned tab to a Misc tab moves the root to the Misc parent
R5 lists the drive roots through explorer_drives
R5 Up climbs a Misc folder one level at a time until the drive list
R5 a Misc file at the root of a drive reaches the drive list in one Up
R4/R5 a change of view, app or active tab discards Up navigation and returns to the automatic root
R5 a Misc root offers Up that climbs to the drive list
A4 with no apps saved the sidebar still shows the Files section
R5: an app-owned active tab roots at the app root, and switching to a Misc tab roots at that file's parent
R5: a Misc file in a deep path roots at its parent folder, not the home folder
R5: a Misc file at a drive root roots at the drive and Up reaches the drive list
A4: a loose file still gets the sidebar and its Files section
A4: with no apps saved the sidebar still shows the Files section

requirements.text: The command palette offers an 'Open file…' entry in every view. Choosing it launches the operating system file picker; the chosen files open in the editor and the main area switches to the editor view. The editor's existing Open… toolbar button, Ctrl+O shortcut and empty-state 'Open a file…' button keep launching the same picker.
tests: R1: the home view offers it and choosing it opens the picked file in the editor view
R1: the entry is present in the app view too, and cancelling leaves the view and tabs unchanged
R1: picking several files opens each one
R1: opening a file while another tab has unsaved text keeps that text
R1: the editor's Open. button, Ctrl+O and the empty-state button still run the same picker

requirements.text: The sidebar contains a Files explorer section beside the apps list (a second section or a tab; the layout is the builder's choice). It shows a tree that loads one directory level at a time: clicking a folder expands or collapses it, and its children are fetched only when it is first expanded. By default the tree hides the folders named node_modules, .git, target and dist; a Show hidden control reveals them and hides them again. A folder that cannot be read appears as locked and does not raise an error.
tests: R2: a file row stays memoised, so an unrelated App update does not re-render every file

requirements.text: Clicking a file in the explorer opens it through the editor's existing open path and switches the main area to the editor view. If the file is already open, its existing tab is focused instead of opening a second tab. Images and other preview-kind files follow the editor's existing preview handling.
tests: R3: clicking a file opens it through the editor's open path and shows the editor view
R3: clicking an image opens it in the editor's existing preview form, not a text editor
R3: clicking a file that is already open focuses its tab instead of opening a second
R3: a file that fails to open shows the editor's existing error instead of crashing
R3: clicking a folder expands it and never opens it as a file

requirements.text: The explorer root follows where the user is. In the app view the root is the selected app's root. In the editor view it is the root of the app that owns the active editor tab, found with the same path-to-owning-app lookup the tab groups use (the deepest app root that contains the path). The user never chooses a root by hand when an app root applies. Changing the root never closes or changes any open tab.
tests: R4: in the app view it is the selected app's root and follows a newly selected app
R4: in the editor view it is the deepest owning app's root
R4: opening a file under the current root keeps the same owning app, so the root does not jump
R4: an app root that no longer exists shows as unreadable instead of raising

requirements.text: When the active editor tab belongs to no app (the Misc group), for example a loose file opened through 'Edit with Tinkerdeck' from outside every app root, the explorer is rooted at that file's parent folder, and Up climbs the folder hierarchy all the way to the drive list.
